caption:
🏋️‍♀️💻 FITNESS SF, a gym chain in San Francisco, is asking members to stop vibe coding between sets.
A screen inside one of its gyms shows a notice titled "Gym Etiquette 101."
It asks people to keep their rest time for recovery and to stop writing code, checking commits, or prompting AI during their workout.
It ends with "Be present. Lift harder. Ship later."
The locally owned chain, founded in 2012, runs 8 gyms across San Francisco, Oakland, and Marin, in the same region where many of the big AI labs are based.
AI researcher Andrej Karpathy coined the term vibe coding in February 2025.
It means building software by telling an AI model what you want in plain English and accepting the code it writes, often without reading every line.
Many developers now leave coding agents running on tasks for long stretches while they do something else, so a rest period between sets is enough time to check progress and send the next prompt.
